explanation: Parker overruled Lodge only on sufficiency of land description in a pleading tested by demurrer, saying its rule suits contracts. Cheeseman cites Lodge for certainty of description in a contract, a point not negated.

Hans Hagen never cites Alberte; 588 N.W.2d 298 appears only as a mistaken reporter cite for Manco (583 N.W.2d 293), a Minnesota zoning case. No reliance on the reversed Wisconsin decision for any proposition.

Krauss appears only inside a block quotation from New Mexico's Hansen opinion cataloguing intent-rule jurisdictions. The Kansas court surveys approaches and rests on Kansas cases (Geier, Stueve); it does not use Krauss as authority.

Iowa court string-cites Gill as supporting authority that plaintiffs are denied recovery for falls on floors wet from tracked-in rain, a year after Pribble overruled Gill on exactly that point; no mention of Pribble or the overruling.

Kott cites the N.C. Court of Appeals Hurst decision as support on inquiry into objections to appointed counsel, after the N.C. Supreme Court reversed that decision outright (on the larceny/robbery issue); no subsequent history given. Different litigation.

Khan overruled Albrecht's per se rule against vertical maximum price fixing. The Third Circuit cites Albrecht at 150 n.6 only for the point that coerced acquiescence can still be a combination or agreement, which Khan did not disturb.

Pelican relies on League Central, but the excerpted 30 Nov 1987 First Guaranty opinion applies League Central and affirms; from my knowledge the overruling came on rehearing in 1988, after Pelican (15 Dec 1987). Timing limb fails.
